text:
maria: Heads-up — since ~08:10 UTC we're seeing NIC firmware flaps hitting a subset of GPU hosts in az-b. Network flap rate on the node pool jumped from ~0.5% -> ~14% in the last 35m. GPU pods are reporting transient attach failures and KV cache misses.

akshay: Copy. Any clear topology pattern? specific racks or instance types?

maria: Mostly N1 and N2 racks in az-b-east (node labels: zone=az-b rack=6/7). Logs show repeated `link state changed` + `LRO/TSO offload` resets. Not obvious CPU/thermal spikes.

kevin: Marking this as potential NIC firmware regression. We've got similar signatures from the April cluster issue but that was a driver/firmware combo. Did we just get a batch update?

maria: No planned firmware push. Host agent shows `apt-get`/`yum` unchanged. Cloud provider reported a brief control-plane update at ~07:55 UTC for az-b, maybe correlated.

sarah: From an ops perspective we should start soft draining affected racks to prevent noisy eviction backpressure on schedulers. Proposal: cordon the 6 affected hosts, migrate long-lived GPU pods to healthy AZs with capacity buffer, keep < 30% shift per 15m window to avoid a slam on cloud quotas. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

akshay: +1. Can we do weighted traffic steering instead of immediate full shift? For hosted API we should prefer region-level fallback before cross-region to avoid egress costs.

maria: Plan IAW:
- cordon affected nodes (kubectl cordon)
- drain non-critical/gpu-spot pods first with `--grace-period=120`
- mark a temporary routing policy to prefer az-a and az-c for new allocations
- open a limited capacity burst in Dedicated pool if autoscaler needs headroom

Command snippet I'll run:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -l rack=6,zone=az-b -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl cordon {}
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
```

kevin: Add: update placement policy to route new inference requests to model-variant fallback in az-a/az-c for 30m. We'll also enable prefix caching on the remaining AZs to reduce cold-start pressure.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2034-azb-nicflap, severity: high. Pager notified (maria, akshay, sarah).

akshay: Monitoring cues to watch: pod Evicted count, kube-scheduler requeue latency, token generation rate (we saw KV miss storms cause auth spikes), and inter-AZ egress bandwidth. Set alerts for Evicted > 5/min and SchedulerLatency p95 > 450ms.

maria: Observed log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T08:12:14Z] nic0: link state changed: DOWN
[2026-03-18T08:12:17Z] eth0: LRO disabled due to reset
[2026-03-18T08:13:03Z] gpu-driver: attach error: -110
```

sarah: Two operational constraints to call out:
1) Dedicated reserved pools are ~85% utilized this morning; shifting >20% will force us to spin new reserved capacity or fallback to hosted which increases cost.
2) Cross-AZ egress is billed and will add ~0.6c per request for large output workloads. Keep an eye on throughput.

akshay: If we must reassign heavy jobs, prefer quantized model variants to save bandwidth (smaller responses) and enable batching to reduce calls. Also throttle non-prod jobs immediately.

ops-runner: Running cordon for nodes: node-azb-06a, node-azb-06b, node-azb-07a. Drain jobs kicked off in rolling window.

maria: Kicking off canary shift: 15% traffic -> az-a/az-c over next 10m, observe scheduler requeues and latency. If stable, continue +15% next 10m. Rolling plan documented below.

kevin: I'll prepare a rollback plan to re-enable nodes if flap subsides — steps: uncordon, reheat KV cache, restart nic driver on host. We should capture dmesg and `ethtool -S` before restart.

sarah: Action items:
- maria: execute cordon/drain + canary shift (in progress)
- akshay: update alert thresholds and placement policies
- kevin: prep host-level diagnostics and prepare driver restart playbook
- ops-runner: track cost delta from cross-AZ egress and reserved capacity events

maria: Will post status update in 15m. If anyone sees a spike in 5xxs, tag this thread. :thumbsup:
